patch_description: The best prior result (749.49 vs current 1035.14) came from a greedy Steiner-tree heuristic: process destinations in order of decreasing standalone Dijkstra cost, and re-run Dijkstra per destination with dynamic edge weights where already-paid (shared) edges count as free. This builds shared trunk edges early and lets later destinations piggyback at zero marginal cost, minimizing the union of paid edges — which the evaluator charges once globally per (dst, partition)-independent edge. The current program lost that sharing logic. I restore the dynamic re-weighting approach and additionally keep the destination ordering (expensive first) so trunks are built by the destinations that benefit most. I also keep a safe fallback to `shortest_path` for disconnected nodes, preserving the 100% success rate.
